4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.

## 1. Death and life  (`#death-and-life`)

Cited ayat: 2:243

> **2:243** أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمْ وَهُمْ أُلُوفٌ حَذَرَ ٱلْمَوْتِ فَقَالَ لَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مُوتُوا۟ ثُمَّ أَحْيَٰهُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:243): The ayah asks whether one has not considered those who went out from their homes, in the thousands, fearing death.

**c2** (2:243): God said to them: die; then He gave them life.

**c3** (2:243): God has bounty over people, but most people do not give thanks.

### One-minute summary

The ayah speaks of people who went out from their homes in the thousands, fearing death [c1]. God said to them: die; then He gave them life [c2].

### Complete story

The ayah asks whether one has not considered those who went out from their homes, in the thousands, fearing death [c1]. God said to them: die; then He gave them life [c2]. God has bounty over people, but most people do not give thanks [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah is one sentence and carries a series of statements: the going out, the saying of God and then the giving of life, and the remark on thanks [c1][c2][c3]. It gives no names and no setting, so the account is as short as the verse [c1].

### Kids mode

Once some people left their homes, many thousands of them, because they were afraid of dying [c1]. God said to them: die; then He gave them life [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that fear of death is set beside God's power to give life [c1][c2]. Another is that the ayah ends by saying most people do not give thanks for God's bounty [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who these people were, where they lived, why they feared death, and when this was.
- Not established: how they died, how they were given life, or what they did afterwards.
- Not established: whether the words die and then He gave them life describe one event or a manner of speaking; the ayah gives no more.
- The ayah does not say how many thousands.
